title: Fight event dispatch and Replay boxer-identity bridge
confidence: PROBABLE overall; individual facts noted below are direct static observations

generic_event_dispatch.descriptor_behavior: Named event descriptors are resolved/registered by name+hash and dispatched with a caller-built payload.
generic_event_dispatch.handle_note: Callers pass 8-byte event-handle storage, not a numeric event ID. In the debug ELF these handle references are PSP-relocated into segment-1/BSS storage.

dataflow: func_0010BB58 resolves each participating boxer and calls func_0010C9C8 once per boxer.
func_0010C9C8 consumes xdbboxr field 0x05 as a bounded 76-entry selector and returns a normalized code; unmapped cases can fall back through field 0x07's alias-linked path.
func_0010BB58 writes the two normalized results into the Replay payload and calls func_003E5860.
If the dispatcher is not initialized for the event, func_0010BB58 calls func_003E4A94 with descriptor D_0055AB38 and retries.
D_0055AB38 resolves to the literal event name Replay.
replay_event.semantic_boundary: Field 0x05 is proven to feed boxer identity/profile codes in the Replay event payload. This does not prove that the field or normalized code is a commentary/speech/audio ID.

decision_announcement_correction.finding: Decision Announcement Script is one entry in a fight-presentation script-name initializer, not by itself evidence of commentary-audio lookup.

provenance: Derived from static disassembly of the user-provided debug/review BOOT.BIN and cross-checked against the matching retail address family.
No executable or resource bytes are committed.

named_event_registry.correction: Replay is registered out of sequence at runtime handle 0x005AB848 (raw 0x20FA0). RefCountDown begins at 0x005AB850 (raw 0x20FA8), and the later sequence resumes after PunchLanded at UpdateStatus=0x005AB8C0. The initializer 0x001106CC is authoritative.

speech_event_bridge.confidence: CONFIRMED for named event identities and dispatch sites; payload semantics partially unresolved
speech_event_bridge.correction: The TCC diagnostic labels in 0x0013DDC4 do not mean that routine dispatches the TCC event. Relocation-aware handle resolution proves it dispatches NISAdvice.

payload.note: Remaining word semantics are still being traced and are not promoted to names.

aems_to_speech_bridge.confidence: CONFIRMED for callback registration/request layout/byte-range playback arithmetic

request_layout.+0x04: relative byte offset within the event's canonical speech-data entry

byte_range_decoder.behavior: decodes a per-entry byte start and byte length from scaled position entries; the producer can add an additional source-relative byte displacement to the start

final_playback_addressing.formula: final bank byte offset = event-record base .dat offset + request relative byte offset

aems_to_speech_bridge.implication: The speech ABI is now bounded across both sides of the callback: generic AEMS events produce explicit bank/event/range requests, and AuSpeechManager maps those requests to byte ranges in the three speech data banks. What remains is semantic mapping from gameplay/named-event payloads to the AEMS event IDs and bank records.

chant_identity_bridge.confidence: CONFIRMED for dataflow and filename selection; original field/function labels remain partially unresolved
filename_selection: missing per-boxer bank -> Chant_PSP_Gen%03d.abk with randomized ID 100..107
chant_identity_bridge.implication: The same xdbboxr field-0x05-derived normalized boxer identity used in Replay payloads also selects boxer-specific chant audio. Field 0x05 is therefore demonstrably part of boxer audio/presentation identity, but this still does not make it a raw commentary/speech-line ID.

weight_class_audio_bridge.semantic_boundary: The literal Gsmall/Gmed/Glarge filenames and six-class routing are proven. The meaning of the 'G' prefix is not expanded without direct evidence.

callback_dataflow: Generic gameplay event dispatch invokes listener callback(event_payload, listener_context).
0x0049B564 resolves listener_context through 0x004970EC into an AEMS mapping record.
The callback allocates 4 + 4*N bytes, where N is record byte +0x0B.
Packet word 0 receives the 4-byte AEMS mapping key; N payload words are copied from the generic gameplay-event payload into packet+4.
0x004974CC accepts/submits the packet into the AEMS active-state machinery.
If submission fails the callback frees the packet; a successful result transfers ownership.

mapping_key.note: 0x00497090 selects one of up to eight mapping descriptors by the two category bytes; 0x00497048 resolves the 16-bit selector within that descriptor.

generic_event_to_aems_bridge.implication: Named gameplay events are not merely parallel to AEMS. Parsed AEMS bank entries actively subscribe to Fight Night's generic event bus, and fired gameplay-event payloads are converted into AEMS command packets. This closes the high-level generic-event -> AEMS boundary.
